name: Al Nakheel and the Corniche
tagline: The city centre along the creek, with the shops and the souks
description: The commercial heart of the emirate on the eastern side of the creek, with the malls, the banks, the gold and fish souks and the corniche walk along the water. It is the practical centre of Ras Al Khaimah, where residents shop and where the rental supply is widest.
bestFor: Anyone who wants shops, services and the creek walk close by
pros: All shopping, banks and services in one area
Widest rental supply in the emirate
cons: Traffic and no walkability beyond the corniche

name: Al Marjan Island
tagline: The reclaimed islands, resorts and new apartment towers
description: Four coral-shaped reclaimed islands off the coast holding the emirate's resort development and its newest residential towers, with private beaches and the casino resort under construction that has driven a great deal of the recent building. Modern, well-serviced and priced at the top of the local market.
bestFor: Stays wanting a new apartment with a beach below it
cons: The highest rents in the emirate

name: Al Hamra Village
tagline: The marina and golf community south of the city
description: A planned residential community around a marina, a golf course and a beach, twenty minutes south of the centre, with townhouses and low-rise apartments aimed at long-term residents rather than tourists. It has its own mall and school and functions as a self-contained suburb.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a settled community with a beach and a marina
pros: Marina, golf and beach within the community
More community feel than the towers
cons: Twenty minutes from the city centre
Compound living is not for everyone

name: Al Dhait and the Inland Districts
tagline: Where residents live, away from the water
description: The residential districts inland from the creek, with ordinary apartment blocks, local supermarkets, and a population that is largely South Asian and Egyptian working in the emirate's industries. Rents here are a fraction of the coastal developments and this is where the value is for a long stay.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: The lowest rents in the emirate by a wide margin
Local shops and food at genuine local prices
A year-round community rather than a resort
cons: Fifteen minutes from anything on the water

name: Jebel Jais Road
tagline: Up the mountain, the country's highest point
description: The road climbing the Hajar mountains behind the city to just under 1,900m, with a viewing platform, the world's longest zip line, hiking and via ferrata routes, and air cool enough to need a jacket when the coast is at forty. Accommodation is limited to a camp and a few lodges near the top.
bestFor: Weekends and escapes from the summer heat rather than a base
pros: The only genuinely cool air in the emirate
Hiking, via ferrata and the zip line
cons: Forty-five minutes up from the city and a car is essential
Nothing to do beyond the outdoors
